1. `git fetch origin`; create `integration/final` from `origin/refactor/compose-outcomes`; merge the three fix branches (merge commits, no rebase, no force-push); resolve conflicts keeping every side's intent (expected: `napi/*`, changesets, `docs/spec/06-decisions.md` and `04`).

3. Investigate the failed macOS x86_64 NAPI job that was seen on PR #122 (`gh pr checks 122`, `gh run view <id> --log-failed`): decide if it is infrastructure (runner timeout) or real; report with evidence.
4. Consistency sweep of the combined result: stale mentions of deleted or renamed APIs (`render_toon`/`render_kv` on AgentResponse, `empty_state`, `michi_core::Error`, `OpRef`, `render_parts`, `ToonOptions::total_count`, `JsonObject::new`, `.hints` on ToonOptions) in docs, README, rustdoc, examples, benches, scripts, packages/michi-node README; changesets that contradict each other or the final behavior (fix wording; keep one `Breaking:` paragraph per distinct break); ADR index and spec README status lines.

Revert incidental rewrites of `fuzz/Cargo.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` unless a real dependency changed.
6. Push `integration/final` and open ONE draft PR to main: `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1 gh pr create --draft --base main --head integration/final --title "refactor: core hardening (envelope integrity, NAPI structure, redaction, API invariants, composed outcomes)" --body ... < /dev/null` (plain `gh pr create` hangs on a prompt; do not use the API). # Shared brief: michi hardening trails (read fully)

Repo /Users/gabe/Projects/michi (Rust workspace; `michi-core` FSL, `michi-graph` MIT no_std, `michi-pipeline` async, NAPI shim in `packages/michi-node`, its exports in `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs`). 0.10.0 is released; we are pre-1.0 and every consumer is our own repo, so **breaking changes are fine and legacy surface is removed, never shimmed**. Follow `AGENTS.md` and `PRINCIPLES.md`; ADRs and `docs/spec/06-decisions.md` record decisions you must not re-litigate (read headings first).
Four read-only audits produced the findings you act on: `/tmp/claude-501/audit-{architecture,security,rust-perf,duplication}.md`. Your trail names the finding numbers; read those entries (evidence, proposed change, "Not examined") and verify each is still true on current main before changing code. If a finding is wrong or already fixed, say so and skip it.

## Parallel trails, strict ownership (this is how we avoid conflicts)
Other trails run at the same time in other worktrees. Edit only files your trail owns. If your change forces a one-line call-site fix in a file another trail owns (for example `napi.rs`), make the minimal fix and say so in your report. Never reformat or reorganize files you do not own. If `git merge origin/main` brings conflicts in your files, resolve them keeping both sides' intent.
Trails: T1 envelope integrity (core model files, toon/ writers); T2 NAPI structure (`napi.rs` and `packages/michi-node`); T3 release-signing CI (`.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, `.prototools`); T4 pipeline error redaction (`crates/michi-pipeline/src/error.rs`, `redact.rs`, `fuzz/`, trust-model docs); T5 docs/tests/CI hygiene (docs drift, new tests, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`); T6 pipeline observers.

## Flow (autonomous; never ask questions; decide and report the decision)
1. `git fetch origin && git checkout -B <your-branch> origin/main` (git network and cargo need `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on that one command; use `$TMPDIR` for temp files; keep commands simple, no computed git arguments).
2. TDD: a failing test first, confirm it fails for the right reason, then fix. For every behavioral claim, break the code on purpose (mutant), watch the test fail, revert. Report the mutants.
3. Update docs/spec for anything you change (CI's "Spec first" job) and rustdoc for every pub item. Add one `.changeset/<slug>.md` for code changes (look at existing ones and `CONTRIBUTING.md`; package `michi-core` unless your change is elsewhere; start a paragraph with `Breaking:` when behavior or API breaks). No changeset for CI-only or docs-only changes.
4. Checks, judged by exit code only: `just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust`, `just typos`, plus `just check` once at the end, plus anything specific to your trail (Node: `pnpm build && pnpm test` in `packages/michi-node`; workflows: `actionlint` and `just zizmor`).
5. Commit (conventional, why-not-what; **no claude.ai session links, no Claude-Session trailer**), push, open a **draft** PR against main with a short plain body (what, why, how checked, what was not run, any decision you made). Never merge, never force-push, never push to main.

## Final message (<= 200 words)
PR URL; per-finding outcome (fixed / skipped with reason); decisions you made; checks with exit codes; mutants run; anything left or surprising.

docs/spec/03-rust-api.md:396:- Section names and KV keys are root keys, beside the names michi writes itself. Those are one reserved list shared by every writer: `totalCount`, `help`, `recovery`, `truncated`, `budget`, `sections`, `provenance`, and the error document's `error`, `message`, `causes` and `exit_code`, reserved even on success so caller data cannot render an error document while `isError` is false. Validity never depends on caller data: a reserved name, two blocks writing one root key, two failed sections (each would write `error`), or two equal provenance labels (or a label `fingerprint`, with or without a fingerprint) renders the whole body as the `toon_validation_failed` (or `kv_validation_failed`) error naming the key (a cause of the caller's error when the response has one), the JSON `error` object says the same, and `is_error()`, the JSON `isError` and MCP `isError` are true. The JSON `sections` still carry the data as given.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:873:- **The caller's error is never hidden.** A `DomainError` and a validation failure (an invalid section, or two blocks writing one root key) used to collide on the key `error`, so the text read `error: toon_validation_failed` with "duplicate root key 'error'", a key the caller never used, while the JSON still said `external_failure`. Now the caller's error leads on every surface and stays the JSON `error` (code, message, `retryable`); the failure is added as its last cause, `<code>: <message>`, the form the NAPI exports throw, and a failed section writes no lines of its own. A collision still drops the sections, so the body is the error block alone. `isError` stays true. Considered: putting the failure first and the caller's error in its causes (the agent would read michi's bug before the tool's real failure, and `retryable` would be lost), and a separate root key for the failure (a twelfth reserved key and a second error shape). The failure is a cause because it is one more thing that went wrong with this answer, and the shape already carries a list of them.

content.content:
---
michi-core: minor
michi-pipeline: minor
michi-node: minor
---

michi-core: a value's rules now hold for its whole life, because the types with a rule across their fields keep those fields private. A `RetryConfig` can no longer get a zero `max_delay` after `try_new`, which turned a server's `Retry-After: 60` into an immediate retry. A `DomainError` can no longer have its code or retry flag changed behind the builder, which left a retryable timeout without its "verify first" hint. A `PartialSuccess` can no longer list one operation as both completed and failed. `CallToolResult.structured_content` is now an `Option<JsonObject>`, checked when it is built in every build, so every result serializes. The wire output is unchanged.

Breaking: `DomainError`'s fields are private. Read them with `code()`, `message()`, `causes()`, `hints()`, `get_recovery()`, `get_retry_after()` and `is_retryable()`, and use `class()` to classify. `render()` and `render_json()` are now `render(OutputFormat::Text)` and `render(OutputFormat::Json)`. `retry_after` takes `impl Into<Option<Duration>>`, and the new `context(prefix)` replaces writing to `message`. `michi_core::Error` and `michi_core::Result` are removed; nothing in michi produced them. `RetryConfig`'s fields are private; read them with `max_retries()`, `base_delay()`, `max_delay()` and `jitter_factor()`, and build one with `new`, `try_new` or `default`. `PartialSuccess::new` is now `PartialSuccess::try_new`, which returns `DuplicateOpIndex` when an index repeats. Its fields are read with `completed()`, `failed()` and `skipped()`. `OpRef` is split into `CompletedOp` (no reason) and `SkippedOp`. `Pipeline` has no `id`, so `Pipeline::new(steps)` takes only the steps. `CallToolResult::new` takes `Option<JsonObject>`; `CallToolResult::try_new` is removed (use `JsonObject::try_new`). `StatusResponse::with_hints` is renamed `hints`, and `render_already_done` takes `&[Hint]`.

Also: `ErrorCode` and `ErrorClass` implement `Hash`, `ErrorCode` implements `Display` (its label), and `DomainError` implements `PartialEq`.

michi-pipeline: `StepId` and `RunId` implement `FromStr` and `Borrow<str>`, so `"fetch".parse::<StepId>()` works and a map keyed by id can be looked up with a `&str`. `AttemptRecord` implements `Eq`. `RunRecord::to_pipeline()` no longer carries the run id (read it with `run_id()`). An ambiguous timeout's `DomainError` now carries one verify-first hint, not none: the conversion used to write `retryable = false` past the builder and so dropped core's hint.

michi-node: Breaking: `renderPartialSuccess` takes `CompletedOp[]` and `SkippedOp[]` in place of `OpRef[]`. It throws when an `index` appears twice across the three lists, and when a completed operation has a `reason`. Before, a duplicate rendered as two outcomes and the reason was dropped without a word.

Migration: replace `e.code`, `e.message`, `e.retryable` and the other field reads with the getters. Replace `e.render()` with `e.render(OutputFormat::Text)`, and replace `cfg.max_delay` and the other config fields with `cfg.max_delay()`. Replace `PartialSuccess::new(c, f, s)` with `PartialSuccess::try_new(c, f, s)?`, `OpRef::new` with `CompletedOp::new` or `SkippedOp::new`, and `Pipeline::new(id, steps)` with `Pipeline::new(steps)`. Wrap structured content as `Some(JsonObject::try_new(text)?)`. Replace `michi_core::Error::Domain(e)` with `e`.
---
michi-core: minor
michi-pipeline: minor
michi-node: minor
---

michi-core: every outcome composes into one `AgentResponse`. `error(DomainError)` adds the error block, which renders first, and `partial_success(name, ps)`, `status(s)`, `pipeline(name, p)` and `already_done(operation, summary)` add sections. Their hints and recovery hints join the response's one `help` and `recovery` block. A batch with results, per-op outcomes and an error is now one valid TOON document, one JSON object and one MCP result. NAPI: `AgentResponse` gains `error`, `partialSuccess`, `pipeline`, `status` and `alreadyDone`, so `renderJson()` and `toCallToolResult()` now cover errors too.

michi-core: Breaking: one error JSON shape. `DomainError::render(OutputFormat::Json)`, its serde form and its `schemars` schema are the response envelope: `{"body", "error": {"code", "message", "causes", "retryable"}, "hints", "recovery", "isError"}`. `recovery` is always an array, as in every response. Before, the JSON was `{isError, error, message, causes, retryable, hints, recovery}`, with `error` the code and `recovery` an object or `null`. Read `error.code` where you read `error`, and `recovery[0]` where you read `recovery`. The text render is unchanged.

michi-core: Breaking: `PartialSuccess::render` is one table, `partial_success[N]{index,operation,status,reason}:`, with a row per operation sorted by index. Before, it wrote a quoted summary line and separate `completed`, `failed` and `skipped` tables. The failed operations' recovery table is unchanged. An empty report renders `partial_success: []` and `totalCount: 0`. JS `renderPartialSuccess` renders the same.

michi-core: Breaking: an empty `Pipeline` renders `step: []` and `totalCount: 0`, and a `StatusResponse` with no items renders `items: []` and `totalCount: 0`. This is the same empty list as any other section. `michi-pipeline`'s `RunRecord::render` of a run with no steps changes with it.
---
michi-core: minor
michi-node: minor
---

michi-core: what a response reports about itself now has one source each, so its text and JSON cannot contradict each other. A section's `truncated` is derived (its total is above its count), the budget's `sections[n]` roll-up is written from the response's own sections, and the budget's `truncated` is also true whenever a section was cut. The root keys michi writes itself are one reserved list for every writer, and it now includes the error document's keys, so a successful response can no longer render an `error:` / `message:` document from caller data. A provenance label `fingerprint` is always rejected, because it read exactly like the real fingerprint.

Breaking: `Section`'s fields are private; read them with `name()`, `body()`, `count()`, `total()` and `truncated()`. `Section::truncated(bool)` and `Section::returned_count(n)` are removed; a text section that stands for several items is `Section::text_with_count(name, body, n)`, and `SectionBody::Text` is now `Text { text, count }`. `SectionCost` and `BudgetSummary::section()` are removed, and the budget's JSON no longer has a `sections` array (the response's `sections` carries those counts). `truncated_section` now takes `(name, fields, &outcome, row, guidance)` and builds the rows from `outcome.kept`. `budget`, `sections`, `provenance`, `truncated`, `error`, `message`, `causes` and `exit_code` join `totalCount`, `help` and `recovery` as reserved: as a type name (`render_toon`, `list`, `empty_state`), a KV key (`render_kv`, `kv_items`) or a section name they are a validation error, and the error messages list the reserved keys.

Migration: `.truncated_section(Section::toon(name, f, rows), &outcome, g)` becomes `.truncated_section(name, f, &outcome, |item| row_of(item), g)`. Drop `.truncated(..)` on sections and `.section(SectionCost::new(..))` on budgets. Rename any KV key or list named after a reserved key (for example a `message` field becomes `commit_message`). In JavaScript, `renderKv`, `renderToon`, `emptyState` and `kvItems` reject the same reserved names.
---
michi-core: minor
---

michi-core: Breaking: `ToonOptions` is the list alone. `hints`, `total_count` and `truncation_hint` (and their builders) are removed; `totalCount`, `help[]` and the truncation hint belong to `AgentResponse`, which places each once for the whole response. `render_toon` writes the list entry and the `truncated` block. `render_kv(items)` lost its `total_count` and `hints` parameters. NAPI: `renderToon` no longer takes `totalCount`, `hints` or `truncationHint`, and `renderKv(items)` no longer takes `totalCount` or `hints`; `AgentResponse.items`, `kvItems` and `truncationHint` keep them.

Migration: `render_toon(&ToonOptions::new(..).total_count(Some(n)).hints(h))` becomes `AgentResponse::new(name).section(Section::toon(name, fields, rows).total_count(Some(n))).hint(..)` rendered with `render(OutputFormat::Text)`. For hints on a standalone list, `append_hints(&mut out, &hints)`.

michi-core: Breaking: one definitive empty state. `empty_state`, `empty_state_with_hints`, `try_empty_state`, `try_empty_state_with_hints`, the `empty` module and NAPI `emptyState` and `emptyStateWithHints` are removed. An empty `Toon` section, and so an untouched `AgentResponse`, now renders `name: []` and `totalCount: 0` (it rendered `name: []` alone). Use `AgentResponse::new(name)` (plus `.hint(..)`) where you called `empty_state`. An empty `Kv` section still renders nothing.

michi-core: `AgentResponse::render`, `is_error()` and `to_call_tool_result()` no longer copy every row on each call. They validate and render a borrowed view of the section's rows: 1,000 rows took 2,015 allocations to render and 2,011 for `is_error()`, and now take about what `render_toon` takes. `toon::list` no longer keeps every parsed item until the rows are built. Output is unchanged.

michi-core: Breaking: `PartialSuccess::render` is one table, `partial_success[N]{index,operation,status,reason}:`, with a row per operation sorted by index. michi-core: minor
michi-node: minor

michi-core: what a response reports about itself now has one source each, so its text and JSON cannot contradict each other. A section's `truncated` is derived (its total is above its count), the budget's `sections[n]` roll-up is written from the response's own sections, and the budget's `truncated` is also true whenever a section was cut. In JavaScript, `renderKv`, `renderToon`, `emptyState` and `kvItems` reject the same reserved names.
---
michi-core: minor
---

michi-core: Breaking: `ToonOptions` is the list alone. `hints`, `total_count` and `truncation_hint` (and their builders) are removed; `totalCount`, `help[]` and the truncation hint belong to `AgentResponse`, which places each once for the whole response. `render_toon` writes the list entry and the `truncated` block. `render_kv(items)` lost its `total_count` and `hints` parameters. NAPI: `renderToon` no longer takes `totalCount`, `hints` or `truncationHint`, and `renderKv(items)` no longer takes `totalCount` or `hints`; `AgentResponse.items`, `kvItems` and `truncationHint` keep them.

Migration: `render_toon(&ToonOptions::new(..).total_count(Some(n)).hints(h))` becomes `AgentResponse::new(name).section(Section::toon(name, fields, rows).total_count(Some(n))).hint(..)` rendered with `render(OutputFormat::Text)`. For hints on a standalone list, `append_hints(&mut out, &hints)`.

michi-core: Breaking: one definitive empty state. `empty_state`, `empty_state_with_hints`, `try_empty_state`, `try_empty_state_with_hints`, the `empty` module and NAPI `emptyState` and `emptyStateWithHints` are removed. An empty `Toon` section, and so an untouched `AgentResponse`, now renders `name: []` and `totalCount: 0` (it rendered `name: []` alone). Use `AgentResponse::new(name)` (plus `.hint(..)`) where you called `empty_state`. An empty `Kv` section still renders nothing.

michi-core: `AgentResponse::render`, `is_error()` and `to_call_tool_result()` no longer copy every row on each call. They validate and render a borrowed view of the section's rows: 1,000 rows took 2,015 allocations to render and 2,011 for `is_error()`, and now take about what `render_toon` takes. `toon::list` no longer keeps every parsed item until the rows are built. Output is unchanged.

michi-core: Breaking: the NAPI byte budget is now 16 MiB, was 64 MiB, per call and per `AgentResponse`. It limited input only, and a render writes up to 19 times the bytes it holds (a control character is 6 bytes in the text, 13 in the JSON, 19 in `toCallToolResult()`). At 64 MiB a maximal response took 3.2 GiB and 25 s in `toCallToolResult()`, and a `renderJson()` over V8's string limit failed only after it was rendered. At 16 MiB every render is under that limit, so a response renders or is rejected before anything is rendered. In JavaScript, a call with more than 16 MiB of strings, or an `AgentResponse` that would hold more, now throws `input byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216` or `cumulative byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216` where up to 64 MiB was accepted. Every other limit, error message and TypeScript type is unchanged.

michi-core: Breaking: `michi_core::napi` (behind the `napi` feature) now exposes only `num`. The typed functions `render_toon(JsToonOptions)`, `render_hints`, `append_hints`, `render_recovery`, `render_kv`, `render_status`, `render_domain_error`, `render_already_done`, `render_partial_success`, `render_pipeline`, `already_done`, `empty_state_with_hints` and the `JsAgentResponse` Rust methods are private; the JS exports are the only entry points. `napi.rs` is split by concern into `napi/*.rs`.

michi-core: `ErrorCode` gains `ALL` and `FromStr`, and `StepStatus` gains `ALL` and `from_labels` (with `StepLabelError`): the inverse of `label()` and `reason()`, built from the same tables.
---
michi-core: minor
---

michi-core: Breaking: the NAPI byte budget now charges a name for every place a render writes it, so the 16 MiB cap bounds the output as it said it did. A `truncated` row repeats the cell's field name, and the section name when two or more sections are cut, for every cut cell, and the `totalCount` table repeats the section name, but each was charged once. A 4 KiB field name with 1,000 rows of one 201-char cell held 261 KB and rendered to 95 times that in text and 112 times in JSON, and at 60,000 rows `renderText()` failed with `Failed to convert rust String into napi string`. In JavaScript, `AgentResponse.items`, `partialSuccess`, `pipeline`, `status` and `renderToon` now charge a field name (and a section name) once for each string cell over 200 chars, `partialSuccess` and `pipeline` charge their section name twice (its header and its `totalCount` row), and `hint` and `recoveryHint` charge 1 and 4 bytes more than their text. A call or response past 16 MiB throws `input byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216` or `cumulative byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216`, where that hostile 60,000-row table was accepted. Normal responses (short names, cells under 200 chars) are charged almost the same as before. A render is at most 19 times the bytes held plus 4 KiB on every surface, and tests measure it over a matrix of hostile responses.
---
michi-core: minor
michi-pipeline: minor
---

Breaking: converting an `ExecutionError` to a `DomainError` no longer puts step text in the trusted `message`. The message is now fixed text (`http 502`, `the step reported an error`, `step panicked`, `deadline passed`), and what the step or server said (an HTTP body, a `failed()` message, a panic payload) is one entry in `causes`, redacted and cut to 512 bytes. Read it from `causes`, not `message`.

`DomainError::from_error` and `from_error_with_causes` now use the new `michi_core::redact::redact_common_shapes`. On top of URL userinfo it redacts the value of `token=`, `access_token=`, `api_key=`, `password=` and similar pairs, and `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `npm_`, `pypi-` and `Bearer` tokens. `redact_url_userinfo` also handles JSON-escaped (`https:\/\/`) and percent-encoded (`https%3A%2F%2F`) URLs and a `"` inside a password. This is best effort: the docs now list what is and is not covered.
---
michi-core: minor
michi-pipeline: patch
---

`redact_common_shapes`, and so `DomainError::from_error` and the pipeline error conversion, now redacts values it used to leave: the credential after a scheme word (`Authorization: Basic ...`, `Bearer`, `Token`, `Digest`), quoted values (`token="x"`, `'x'`, JSON `"password": "x"`, JSON-escaped `\"x\"`), `Key: value` headers (`X-Api-Key:`, `Cookie:`, `Set-Cookie:`), and values after the fullwidth `＝` and `：`. Text that has `token: ...` or similar in prose is redacted too, which is the safe direction. A long line of `key="` pairs no longer takes quadratic time.

`redact_secrets` copies an existing `[REDACTED]` through, so a secret such as `RED` no longer turns the marker into `[[REDACTED]ACTED]` on a second pass; redacting twice is a no-op unless a secret contains `[`.

Step text in a converted `ExecutionError` is now at most 512 bytes including the `…` marker (it was 515).
---
michi-core: minor
michi-node: minor
---

michi-core: Breaking: a validation failure no longer hides the caller's error. A response with `error(e)` and an invalid section (or two blocks writing one root key) used to render `error: toon_validation_failed` with "duplicate root key 'error'" in the text while its JSON still said `e`'s code. Now `e` leads on every surface (text, JSON, `render_for`, `to_call_tool_result`, NAPI) and stays the JSON `error`, and the failure is added as its last cause, `toon_validation_failed: <message>`. `isError` stays true. Several failures (two failed sections, or a failed section beside a collision) are one `error` object too: the caller's error, or without one the first failure, with every other failure as a cause, never a collision on `error`.

michi-core: Breaking: a validation failure is an `error` object in JSON, `{"code": "toon_validation_failed", "message": …, "causes": [], "retryable": false}` (or `kv_validation_failed`), the same keys as every other error. Before, it was `isError: true` with no `error` object. The text is unchanged.

michi-core: Breaking: a section's JSON `totalCount` follows the text's rule. It appears when the total exceeds the rows and is `0` for an empty list, and is left out for a total at or below the rows (it was the declared value whenever one was set). The budget roll-up's `total` column follows the same rule, so it shows `null` where it showed a total equal to the rows, and `0` for an empty list. `Section::total()` still returns the value as given.

michi-core: Breaking: `AgentResponse::hints(vec)` replaces only the hints added with `hint()` and `hints()`. A `status()` report's hints and a `truncated_section()`'s `showing N of M` line are kept; before, `hints()` dropped them.

michi-core: Breaking: `JsonObject::new` is renamed `JsonObject::try_new`, since it can fail. `"…".parse::<JsonObject>()` is unchanged.

# michi — Agent Instructions

## Commands

- Always prefix shell commands with `rtk`.
- `just test` — run all tests (Rust + Node)
- `just test-rust` — Rust tests only (cargo nextest)
- `just check` — fmt + clippy (`--all-targets`, single workspace-wide invocation, matches CI) + rustdoc with warnings denied + fuzz targets build + deny + typos + markdown fmt
- `just pre-push` — fmt-check + `lint-affected` (moon-detected affected crates only, one multi `-p` clippy invocation — not the full workspace)
- `just build-node` — compile NAPI binary for local platform
- `just bench` — run divan benchmarks
- `just snapshots` — review insta snapshot diffs
- `just coverage` — generate lcov.info

## Non-negotiables

- No `unwrap()`/`expect()` in lib code (tests OK with message)
- No `unsafe` outside napi boundary
- `BTreeMap` for output maps, `HashMap` for internal state only
- Pre-allocate strings with `String::with_capacity`
- Truncation uses char boundaries (`floor_char_boundary`)
- Every `pub` item has a doc comment
- NAPI: `version = "3"`, `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` on every export
- Benchmarks: divan (not criterion)
- Tests: `cargo nextest run` (not `cargo test`)

## Testing

- A claim needs a test that fails when the claim breaks. Check by breaking the code on purpose (a mutant) and watching the test fail, then revert.
- Performance: no CI gate on absolute time or percent change (shared runners are too noisy to mean anything). `crates/*/tests/scaling.rs` check the complexity class instead: 10x the input must not take 30x as long (linear ~10x, quadratic ~100x). Add a case there when you add or document a linear-time path. `just bench` is for looking at constant factors by hand.

## Writing

- Write docs in plain, concise language. Keep them friendly and scannable; remove filler and AI-sounding prose.
- Comments should explain non-obvious choices, stay useful, and wrap at 120 columns.

## Philosophy

- Before adding a new primitive or judging whether work is "done," read `PRINCIPLES.md` — the inclusion checklist and process conventions this project runs on.

## Architecture

- Virtual Cargo workspace: the root `Cargo.toml` has no `[package]` and no shared version; Callisto writes each crate's `version` and keeps `michi-core`, `michi-graph`, `michi-pipeline` and the npm package equal (fixed group `michi`, lockstep releases, checked by CI version-sync)
- `crates/michi-core/` — pure sync rendering library, every primitive (default features: only `thiserror` + `compact_str`). Integration tests, divan benches and examples live in `crates/michi-core/{tests,benches,examples}` (`cargo run -p michi-core --example basic_toon`)
- `crates/michi-graph/` — **MIT**, no dependencies, `no_std` + `alloc`: deterministic dependency graphs (`GraphBuilder` → `Graph` → `Dag`; validation reports every problem at once; topological order, layers, ready sets, closures; `Dag<K, E>` keeps edge kinds for `ready_by_edge`). Depends on nothing in michi, releases with the fixed group, and must never gain a non-permissive dependency (`just check-graph-license`). API: `docs/spec/09-graph.md`.
- `crates/michi-pipeline/` — async pipeline execution (shipped): validated `Plan` of `ExecStep`s, `execute`/`resume` returning a `RunRecord`, keyed `BreakerRegistry`, retry budget, per-key concurrency limits, deadline groups, `poll_step`, `step_blocking`, `CancellationToken` (wraps tokio-util), `StepObserver`, its own `ExecutionError` (converts into `DomainError`, not a variant of it — see `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`). API: `docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md`. Depends on `michi-core` (exact `=` version pin), `michi-graph` (exact `=` pin; no michi-graph type in its public API) + `tokio` + `tokio-util`; not re-exported through `michi-core`.
- `packages/michi-node/` — thin NAPI cdylib shim (`publish = false`), npm package name `@orin-dx/michi`; the exports themselves live in `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs` behind michi-core's `napi` feature and are re-exported via `pub use michi_core::napi::*;`
- Published crates: `michi-core`, `michi-pipeline` and `michi-graph`. There is no `michi` crate (the name on crates.io belongs to an unrelated project)
- Feature flags (on `michi-core`): `napi`, `serde` (opt-in Serialize/Deserialize + `toon::list()`), `schemars`, `miette`. Execution layers (`pipeline`, `fuzzy`, `cache`, `cli`) land as separate crates, never as features here — `michi-pipeline` shipped this way (see above); `fuzzy`/`cache`/`cli` are not built anywhere. See `docs/spec/01-overview-and-setup.md`'s Cargo.toml section for the current split.
- See `docs/spec/06-decisions.md` and `docs/adr/README.md` for decisions (`docs/superpowers/` is historical)
- See `docs/spec/` for full module API reference

## Module guide

All modules live in `crates/michi-core/src/`.

| Module | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `toon` | TOON list rendering — token-optimized agent list format |
| `kv` | Key-value single-item rendering |
| `hints` | `help[]` hint blocks |
| `truncate` | Token-safe content truncation |
| `truncation` | `TruncationOutcome`: what a cap on a list cut, however the caller chose the survivors |
| `error` | `DomainError` (with `ErrorCode`/`ErrorClass`): the one agent-facing error, with agent rendering |
| `idempotency` | Partial-success reporting (`PartialSuccess`/`FailedOp`) — despite the name, idempotency keys and already-done detection live in `resilience` (`AlreadyDone`/`already_done()`), not here |
| `resilience` | Retry config, delay calculation, retry-after parsing |
| `redact` | Best-effort redaction: known secrets, URL userinfo and common credential shapes (`redact_common_shapes`); applied by `DomainError::from_error` |
| `status` | Health/status response rendering |
| `recovery` | Recovery hint blocks |
| `response` | `AgentResponse` builder — composes all primitives |
| `section` | `Section` (TOON list, KV or text): one block of a response, with its reported total |
| `budget` | `BudgetSummary`: the budget block and the per-section roll-up |
| `provenance` | Provenance block: where an answer came from |
| `mcp` | MCP `CallToolResult` assembly — always compiled, no feature gate |
| `audience` | `Audience` (assistant/user) — shared by `mcp` and `response::render_for()` |

| `telemetry` | No-op telemetry provider (`NoopProvider`) — zero-cost default, always compiled |
| `napi` | NAPI export surface for `@orin-dx/michi` (`napi` feature only) — the one module allowed `unsafe` |

Write an ADR when a decision changes crate boundaries, dependencies, public contracts, licensing, security, or another cross-cutting constraint. Do not record local implementation choices or every resolved API detail.

Use `Proposed` while a decision is under review and `Accepted` once it is implemented. To change an accepted decision, add a new ADR that names the one it supersedes; preserve the old record. Cite the source and alternatives considered.

docs/spec/06-decisions.md:479:| NAPI 10k × 10 cells sharing one 100 KB JS string | 1.6 s, +11 GiB RSS (copied per cell) | rejected in ~11 ms at 64 MiB (`input byte total …`) |
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:488:- **NAPI budgets:** exports that take collections (`renderToon`, `renderHints`, `appendHints`, `renderRecovery`, `renderKv`, `renderAlreadyDone`, `renderDomainError`, `renderStatus`, `AgentResponse.items`/`kvItems`) take untyped napi values and convert incrementally, because napi-derive converts typed parameters in full before the body runs. Lengths are checked first; then each call gets 1,000,000 cells and 64 MiB of string bytes, with 1 MiB per cell, hint, reason, description or message and 4 KiB per name (type name, field name, key, tool, code, operation, truncation hint). A string's UTF-8 length is charged before it is copied, so shared JS strings cannot amplify. The single-string `AgentResponse` setters keep `String` parameters (napi copies their one argument exactly once) and apply the same caps after the copy. `index.d.ts` declares the same types (`ts_args_type`); the Rust-typed functions keep their names for Rust callers. Considered: checking lengths in the body of the typed exports — rejected, the conversion has already happened by then.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:505:- **Cumulative `AgentResponse` budget (NAPI):** the 64 MiB budget of "Capacity limits" was per call, so a JS `AgentResponse` accepted 65 separate 1 MiB hints and rendered 68,157,514 bytes synchronously. One object now holds at most 64 MiB of caller strings across all its calls. Slots a call replaces (`items`, `kvItems`, `truncationHint`, `humanContent`) give their old bytes back; `hint` and `recoveryHint` add. The error reads `cumulative byte total N exceeds maximum of 67108864`, in the style of `input byte total …`. The constructor's `typeName` (4 KiB), `humanContent` (1 MiB) and `emptyState`'s `typeName` (4 KiB) now have per-string caps too. Considered: counting every byte ever passed — rejected, replacing `items` twice with a 40 MiB list would then fail although the object holds only one list.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:552:- **NAPI coverage:** `renderPartialSuccess`, `renderPipeline` (status and reason as `StepStatus` labels, validated), `emptyStateWithHints` (throws on a reserved type name like `emptyState`) and `alreadyDone` follow the budgeted conversion pattern of "Capacity limits": 10,000 entries per list, 4 KiB per identifier, 1 MiB per name or reason, 64 MiB per call. There is no `truncateInline`: the `truncate` export already is `truncate_inline`.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:598:- **NAPI:** `renderDomainError(code, message, hints, githubAnnotation?, causes?)` — an additive optional trailing array, budgeted like hints (10,000 entries, 1 MiB per cause, counted in the call's 64 MiB). The Rust-typed `napi::render_domain_error` gains a `causes: Vec<String>` parameter (breaking for direct Rust callers of the `napi` module only, allowed in 0.4).
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:799:- **NAPI charges each section.** Every `items` / `kvItems` call costs the type name's bytes plus 64, so empty calls cannot grow a response past the 64 MiB cap.
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:824:- **The byte budget bounds the output (16 MiB, was 64 MiB).** The 64 MiB budget limited input only. A control character renders to 6 bytes in the text, 13 in the JSON and 19 in `toCallToolResult()`, so 64 MiB of input could produce 1.2 GiB, and a `renderJson()` over V8's string limit failed only after it was rendered. Measured in Node before the change (60 one-MiB control-character values): `renderText()` 377 MB, 1.2 GiB RSS, 2.4 s; `renderJson()` rendered, then threw `GenericFailure`, 1.6 GiB RSS; `toCallToolResult()` 25 s, 3.2 GiB. At 16 MiB the worst render is 19 x 16 MiB = 304 MiB, under V8's limit, so a response renders or is rejected by the budget before any rendering. A `const` assertion ties the cap to the string limit, and a unit test pins the factor 19 for every ASCII byte. Considered: charging each control character at its escaped size (exact, but it adds a second accounting table that must follow every escape rule, and plain ASCII gains nothing), and an estimate-then-render check in each render (the budget already is that estimate).
docs/spec/06-decisions.md:825:- **Compatibility:** inputs over 16 MiB of strings per call, or per `AgentResponse`, are now rejected where up to 64 MiB was accepted. Pre-1.0, and no known consumer sends that much; the error names the cap.
docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md:202:- **Output size:** the byte budget bounds what a render writes, not only what it reads. On every surface, a render is at most **19 times the bytes held, plus 4 KiB**. A control character is the worst case for a string: six bytes in the text (`\u0001`), seven in the JSON `body` (the text, escaped again) and six in the raw `sections`, `error` and `hints` copies, so one held byte is at most 6 + 7 + 6 = 19 bytes across the text and the JSON that `toCallToolResult()` returns together. A name is written in more places than that, so the budget charges each name for every place a writer can put it, not once: a `truncated` row writes the cell's field name, and, when two or more sections are cut, its section name, again for every cut cell (a string cell longer than 200 chars; no export changes that cap), so a field name is charged once per cut-capable cell of its column, and the type name or an outcome section's name once per cut-capable cell of its table; a section's name is charged twice (its `name[N]{…}:` header or `name: []` line and its row of the `totalCount` table; the type name's second charge is the one made when the response is built); a hint is charged one byte more than its length and a recovery hint four, for the row and the JSON object that hold them. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fail when a diff changes public Rust API without touching any documentation.

Usage: python3 scripts/check-api-docs.py [BASE [HEAD]] [--pr-body TEXT]

BASE..HEAD defaults to origin/main..HEAD (diffed from their merge base, like a PR). The PR body comes from --pr-body
or the PR_BODY environment variable; a line starting `No spec change needed: <reason>` skips the check.

Public API means added or removed `pub` item lines (fn, struct, enum, trait, type, const, static, mod, use, union,
and `pub name: Type` fields) in crates/*/src/**/*.rs, outside test files and `#[cfg(test)]` modules. Lines that are
identical on both sides (code moved between files) cancel out. Enum variants, trait items and anything a macro
generates are not visible to this check.
"""

import argparse
import collections
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

SRC = re.compile(r"^crates/[^/]+/src/.+\.rs$")
TEST_FILE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(tests?|benches|examples)/|(^|/)tests?\.rs$|_tests?\.rs$")
DOCS = re.compile(r"^(docs/spec/|docs/adr/|crates/[^/]+/README\.md$|README\.md$|ARCHITECTURE\.md$)")
KINDS = "fn|struct|enum|trait|type|const|static|mod|use|union"
ITEM = re.compile(rf'^\s*pub\s+(?:(?:async|const|unsafe|extern\s+"[^"]*")\s+)*(?:{KINDS})\b')
FIELD = re.compile(r"^\s*pub\s+[A-Za-z_]\w*\s*:(?!:)")
ESCAPE = re.compile(r"^No spec change needed:[ \t]*\S", re.MULTILINE)
HUNK = re.compile(r"^@@ -(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@")

input.content:
One PR for the whole core hardening chain, so it can be reviewed and merged once. It replaces the stack #120 to #129 (below). Branch `integration/final` is `refactor/compose-outcomes` (#126) plus the three review-fix branches, merged with merge commits and no conflicts, plus the changes under "Added here".

## What changed, by theme

- **Redaction (#120, #128).** `DomainError::from_error` and the pipeline error conversion redact URL userinfo (also JSON-escaped and percent-encoded), `key=value` pairs (quoted, JSON, fullwidth separators), `Key: value` headers, scheme credentials (`Basic`, `Bearer`, `Token`, `Digest`) and known token shapes, in one linear scan with an exact 512-byte cap. `redact_secrets` is idempotent. Step text no longer goes into the trusted `message`.
- **NAPI structure and budget (#121, #129).** `napi.rs` is split into `napi/*.rs`; `michi_core::napi` exposes only `num`. The byte budget is 16 MiB (was 64 MiB) and charges a name for every place a render writes it, so a render is at most 19 times the bytes held plus 4 KiB on every surface (`napi/cost.rs`, a hostile-matrix test).
- **Envelope integrity (#122).** A response's `truncated`, budget roll-up and reserved root keys each have one source, so text and JSON cannot disagree. `Section`'s fields are private.
- **Legacy removal and render performance (#124).** `ToonOptions` is the list alone; the `empty` module and `empty_state*` are gone (an empty list renders `name: []` and `totalCount: 0`); `AgentResponse::render`, `is_error()` and `to_call_tool_result()` stop copying rows.
- **API invariants (#125).** `DomainError`, `RetryConfig`, `PartialSuccess` and `CallToolResult` keep their cross-field rules behind private fields; `michi_core::Error` is removed.
- **Composed outcomes (#126, #127).** `error`, `partial_success`, `status`, `pipeline` and `already_done` are sections of one `AgentResponse`: one TOON document, one JSON object, one MCP result. The caller's error is never hidden by a validation failure, a validation failure is the same `error` object, a section's total follows one rule, and hints from every source compose.

## Breaking changes a consumer must act on

Rust API:
- `DomainError` fields are private: use `code()`, `message()`, `causes()`, `hints()`, `get_recovery()`, `get_retry_after()`, `is_retryable()`, `class()`. `render()` / `render_json()` become `render(OutputFormat::Text | Json)`. `michi_core::Error` and `Result` are removed.
- `RetryConfig` fields are private (`max_retries()`, `base_delay()`, `max_delay()`, `jitter_factor()`).
- `PartialSuccess::new` is `try_new` (returns `DuplicateOpIndex`); `OpRef` is split into `CompletedOp` and `SkippedOp`; `Pipeline::new(steps)` has no id; `CallToolResult::new` takes `Option<JsonObject>`, and `try_new` is removed; `StatusResponse::with_hints` is `hints`; `render_already_done` takes `&[Hint]`.
- `Section` fields are private (`name()`, `body()`, `count()`, `total()`, `truncated()`); `Section::truncated(bool)`, `returned_count`, `SectionCost` and `BudgetSummary::section()` are removed; `truncated_section(name, fields, &outcome, row, guidance)`.
- `ToonOptions` loses `hints`, `total_count` and `truncation_hint`; `render_kv(items)` loses its `total_count` and `hints` parameters; `empty_state*` and the `empty` module are removed.
- Reserved root keys (`budget`, `sections`, `provenance`, `truncated`, `error`, `message`, `causes`, `exit_code`, plus `totalCount`, `help`, `recovery`) are rejected as type names, KV keys and section names.
- `ExecutionError` to `DomainError`: `message` is fixed text; what the step said is one redacted `causes` entry, 512 bytes at most.
- `AgentResponse::hints(vec)` replaces only the hints added with `hint()` / `hints()`.
- `michi_core::napi` exposes only `num` (the typed Rust functions are private).

JS API (`@orin-dx/michi`):
- A call or `AgentResponse` over 16 MiB of strings throws (`input byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216` / `cumulative byte total ...`); names are charged per place they are written.
- `renderPartialSuccess` takes `CompletedOp[]` and `SkippedOp[]`, and throws on a repeated `index` or a completed operation with a `reason`.
- `renderToon` loses `totalCount`, `hints`, `truncationHint`; `renderKv(items)` loses `totalCount`, `hints`; `emptyState` and `emptyStateWithHints` are removed; reserved names throw. New: `AgentResponse` `error`, `partialSuccess`, `pipeline`, `status`, `alreadyDone`.

Rendered output:
- Error JSON is `{"body", "error": {"code","message","causes","retryable"}, "hints", "recovery", "isError"}` for `DomainError` and for validation failures (`toon_validation_failed` / `kv_validation_failed`); `recovery` is always an array.
- `PartialSuccess::render` is one table `partial_success[N]{index,operation,status,reason}:`; an empty `Pipeline`, `StatusResponse` or `PartialSuccess` renders `[]` and `totalCount: 0`; an empty `Toon` section renders `name: []` and `totalCount: 0`.
- A section's JSON `totalCount` appears only when it exceeds the rows (and is `0` for an empty list); the budget roll-up's `total` is `null` otherwise; the budget JSON has no `sections` array.
- Redacted values in error messages and causes (see Redaction).

## Added here (on top of the three fix branches)

- Two or more failed sections are one `error` object (the first failure, the rest as causes; with a caller's error, the caller's error first and every failure a cause), on every surface, instead of a collision on `error`. Mutants: emitting every failed block's lines, and dropping the causes from the text, each fail `two_failed_sections_are_one_error_object_with_the_second_failure_as_its_cause`.
- The redaction scaling test has a smaller size and a 10 s time limit: a quadratic scan now fails in seconds instead of running for minutes in a debug build (mutants: a per-pair rescan fails on the ratio; a 300x heavier rescan fails on the limit).
- The 17 s output-bound matrix test is one test per character (under 3 s wall time, same cases and same "factor is reached" check; mutant: factor 10 fails it).
- Changesets and docs reconciled: each break stated once against the last release (no `JsonObject::new` rename for a type that is new, no `empty_state` in a changeset that follows its removal, one changeset each for the byte budget and for redaction); stale `michi_core::Error` and `empty` mentions, the spec README module list and the envelope "slice 4" status fixed.

## Review findings fixed

Response consistency (#127): a caller's error hidden by a validation failure; two error JSON shapes; two rules for `totalCount`; `JsonObject::new` that can fail; `hints()` dropping other hint sources; missing scaling cases. Redaction (#128): scheme credentials, quoted values, headers, quadratic scan, 515-byte cap, non-idempotent `redact_secrets`. Output bound (#129): output up to 95 to 112 times the held bytes. Two gaps closed here: two failed sections colliding on `error`, and the redaction scaling test that hung.

## Checks (all exit 0)

`just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust`, `just test-rust-all`, `just test-crates-default`, `cargo test --doc` for michi-core (`serde,schemars,miette`), michi-pipeline (`--all-features`) and michi-graph, `just typos`, `just check` (fmt, clippy, rustdoc, fuzz build, deny, zizmor, typos, markdown fmt), `scripts/check-api-docs.py origin/main HEAD`, the three python script tests, and `pnpm build && pnpm test` in `packages/michi-node` (macOS arm64).

## Not checked

GitHub CI on this branch; `scripts/check-semver.sh` against crates.io; NAPI builds and tests on any platform but local macOS arm64; fuzz targets were built, not run; benchmarks not run. The failed `NAPI (x86_64-apple-darwin)` job on #122 was infrastructure ("The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts", 15 min queue timeout); the same job passed on #126.

## Superseded PRs

#120, #121, #122, #123, #124, #125, #126, #127, #128, #129 (the stack and its fix branches). They are left open and unedited.

## What changed, by theme

- **Redaction (#120, #128).** `DomainError::from_error` and the pipeline error conversion redact URL userinfo (also JSON-escaped and percent-encoded), `key=value` pairs (quoted, JSON, fullwidth separators), `Key: value` headers, scheme credentials (`Basic`, `Bearer`, `Token`, `Digest`) and known token shapes, in one linear scan with an exact 512-byte cap. `redact_secrets` is idempotent. Step text no longer goes into the trusted `message`.
- **NAPI structure and budget (#121, #129).** `napi.rs` is split into `napi/*.rs`; `michi_core::napi` exposes only `num`. The byte budget is 16 MiB (was 64 MiB) and charges a name for every place a render writes it, so a render is at most 19 times the bytes held plus 4 KiB on every surface (`napi/cost.rs`, a hostile-matrix test).
- **Envelope integrity (#122).** A response's `truncated`, budget roll-up and reserved root keys each have one source, so text and JSON cannot disagree. `Section`'s fields are private.
- **Legacy removal and render performance (#124).** `ToonOptions` is the list alone; the `empty` module and `empty_state*` are gone (an empty list renders `name: []` and `totalCount: 0`); `AgentResponse::render`, `is_error()` and `to_call_tool_result()` stop copying rows.
- **API invariants (#125).** `DomainError`, `RetryConfig`, `PartialSuccess` and `CallToolResult` keep their cross-field rules behind private fields; `michi_core::Error` is removed.
- **Composed outcomes (#126, #127).** `error`, `partial_success`, `status`, `pipeline` and `already_done` are sections of one `AgentResponse`: one TOON document, one JSON object, one MCP result. The caller's error is never hidden by a validation failure, a validation failure is the same `error` object, a section's total follows one rule, and hints from every source compose.

## Breaking changes a consumer must act on

Rust API:
- `DomainError` fields are private: use `code()`, `message()`, `causes()`, `hints()`, `get_recovery()`, `get_retry_after()`, `is_retryable()`, `class()`. `render()` / `render_json()` become `render(OutputFormat::Text | Json)`. `michi_core::Error` and `Result` are removed.
- `RetryConfig` fields are private (`max_retries()`, `base_delay()`, `max_delay()`, `jitter_factor()`).

- `Section` fields are private (`name()`, `body()`, `count()`, `total()`, `truncated()`); `Section::truncated(bool)`, `returned_count`, `SectionCost` and `BudgetSummary::section()` are removed; `truncated_section(name, fields, &outcome, row, guidance)`.
- `ToonOptions` loses `hints`, `total_count` and `truncation_hint`; `render_kv(items)` loses its `total_count` and `hints` parameters; `empty_state*` and the `empty` module are removed.
- Reserved root keys (`budget`, `sections`, `provenance`, `truncated`, `error`, `message`, `causes`, `exit_code`, plus `totalCount`, `help`, `recovery`) are rejected as type names, KV keys and section names.
- `ExecutionError` to `DomainError`: `message` is fixed text; what the step said is one redacted `causes` entry, 512 bytes at most.
- `AgentResponse::hints(vec)` replaces only the hints added with `hint()` / `hints()`.
- `michi_core::napi` exposes only `num` (the typed Rust functions are private).

JS API (`@orin-dx/michi`):
- A call or `AgentResponse` over 16 MiB of strings throws (`input byte total N exceeds maximum of 16777216` / `cumulative byte total ...`); names are charged per place they are written.
- `renderPartialSuccess` takes `CompletedOp[]` and `SkippedOp[]`, and throws on a repeated `index` or a completed operation with a `reason`.
- `renderToon` loses `totalCount`, `hints`, `truncationHint`; `renderKv(items)` loses `totalCount`, `hints`; `emptyState` and `emptyStateWithHints` are removed; reserved names throw. New: `AgentResponse` `error`, `partialSuccess`, `pipeline`, `status`, `alreadyDone`.

- A section's JSON `totalCount` appears only when it exceeds the rows (and is `0` for an empty list); the budget roll-up's `total` is `null` otherwise; the budget JSON has no `sections` array.
